answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a bonded stake posted once per agent identity and slashed on duplicate-claim proof. Each operator escrows a fixed deposit before its first reward, and the registry stores one unique key attestation with it. If two identities prove they share an attestation, a fraud proof burns both deposits instead of splitting them. Running N fake personas like a falcon cloning itself across the tundra costs N real deposits at risk, and the attacker loses all of it once collusion surfaces at dawn. Honest operators keep the same small bond, so the rule taxes only fakery.
